diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
index 2530f8f..ca17048 100644
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -20,6 +20,7 @@ user in the ledger file.
 | :- | :- |
 | `member` | open, read, close and export their own accounts; transfer between them |
 | `admin` | everything a member may, plus deposits into any account |
+| `accountant` | read any account and its transfers; change nothing |
 
 ## API
 
diff --git a/src/accounts.js b/src/accounts.js
index bf5c836..6139cee 100644
--- a/src/accounts.js
+++ b/src/accounts.js
@@ -34,9 +34,14 @@ export function listAccounts(store, { ownerId, page = 1 }) {
   return { page, pageSize: PAGE_SIZE, total: mine.length, items: mine.slice(start, start + PAGE_SIZE) }
 }
 
+/** Whether the user may see this account: their own, or any account for an accountant. */
+export function canSee(user, account) {
+  return account.ownerId === user.id || user.role === 'accountant'
+}
+
 export function getOwnAccount(store, user, id) {
   const account = store.get('accounts', id)
-  if (!account || account.ownerId !== user.id) throw new HttpError(404, 'no such account')
+  if (!account || !canSee(user, account)) throw new HttpError(404, 'no such account')
   return account
 }
 
diff --git a/src/auth.js b/src/auth.js
index 76af6f8..c53a31b 100644
--- a/src/auth.js
+++ b/src/auth.js
@@ -1,4 +1,7 @@
 /**
+ * Roles: `member` (own accounts), `admin` (plus deposits), `accountant` (reads
+ * every account's statement, changes nothing).
+ *
  * Bearer tokens. Every request to the API carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`,
  * which names a user in the store. The token is the only credential; it is
  * never logged.
diff --git a/test/server.test.js b/test/server.test.js
index bece284..588b5a0 100644
--- a/test/server.test.js
+++ b/test/server.test.js
@@ -75,3 +75,17 @@ test('an export lands under the export directory, named for the account only', a
     await close()
   }
 })
+
+test('an accountant reads any account and its transfers', async () => {
+  const { dir, store } = await freshStore()
+  store.insert('users', { id: 'usr_eve', name: 'Eve', token: 'tok-eve', role: 'accountant', createdAt: 'now' })
+  const { call, close } = await serve(store, dir)
+  try {
+    const a = await call('POST', '/accounts', { token: 'tok-bob', body: { label: 'A' } })
+    assert.equal((await call('GET', `/accounts/${a.body.id}`, { token: 'tok-eve' })).status, 200)
+    assert.equal((await call('GET', `/accounts/${a.body.id}/transfers`, { token: 'tok-eve' })).status, 200)
+    assert.equal((await call('GET', `/accounts/${a.body.id}`, { token: 'tok-cy' })).status, 404, 'a member still sees only their own')
+  } finally {
+    await close()
+  }
+})

content.text:
Review of PR #5 at `5ff5809` — **complete**, 1 confirmed finding (critical), 0 refuted.

**The defect in one line:** `canSee()` relaxed the ownership check inside `getOwnAccount()`, but that helper gates four routes, not two — the write routes `POST /accounts/:id/close` and `POST /accounts/:id/export` inherit the accountant grant. Sites: `src/accounts.js:42` (the check) and `:48` (`closeAccount`'s call into it); the export route handler in `src/server.js` reaches it the same way. The PR's new test is the blind test that let it through — it asserts only on the two GET routes, so `npm test` passes clean (baseline ran green).

**Budget:** used 12 of 20 agents — 1 scout, 6 finders, 1 triage, 3 skeptics, 1 critic. No ceiling was given, so the script took 20 (room for every fixed angle plus two of the scout's). Nothing was retried, and the same-site check didn't run — triage left a single root cause, so there was nothing to disambiguate.

**Angles:** 6 ran. The scout dropped three with reasons — `migrations-and-rollout` (no migration touched; the role is a string on an existing field), `data-integrity` (no concurrency or caching in the diff), `silent-drops` (no new field written; `role` already round-trips). It sharpened `correctness` and added one of its own, `accountant-write-scope`, which named the shared-helper problem before any finder ran. All six finders independently hit the same defect.

**Verification:** 1 root cause, 1 upheld, 0 refuted. It went to a three-lens panel (critical severity) and 3 of 3 skeptics failed to refute it — one reproduced the close and the export live against a worktree, confirming both the 200s and the on-disk CSV. The verdict is `CONFIRMED`, but the summary and severity were **corrected** by a skeptic during verification (the original finding understated the export half), so it's an upheld-after-correction, not a clean first-pass confirmation. Nothing was dismissed for doubt alone, and nothing came back unverified.

**One gap the critic found, for you to check by hand** — not refuted by anyone, so treat it as a lead rather than a finding: the feature may be unusable for its stated purpose. `GET /accounts` was left untouched and still filters on `ownerId === user.id` (`src/server.js:45` → `src/accounts.js:27`), so an accountant sees `{"total":0,"items":[]}` no matter how many accounts exist — verified empirically by the critic. An accountant can only use the new grant on an account id they already know out-of-band, which defeats a reconciliation role. Every angle on the list points at over-granting; this is an under-grant in an unmodified function, which is why none of them caught it.
